label: prf:q-beta-direction-sanity-gate
title: Proof of q beta direction sanity gate
html:
Proof. Proof of q beta direction sanity gate

Proof

Write q_0 for the substrate modulus, u = b(q)\,\hbar_q^2 for the ladder variable of the precision-ladder factorisation

\mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)
= Q_A(q)\cdot\cos\bigl(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q)\bigr)
  \cdot\prod_{k \ge 2}\bigl(1 + c_k\,u^k\bigr)

(c_2 structural identity), u_0 \approx 8.517\times 10^{-3} for its substrate value, and c_k for the pinned ladder coefficients. A candidate Habiro element F(q) is a proposed closed form for the correction factor \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)/[Q_A(q)\cos(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q))] (c_k recursion), and the target magnitude is

F_{\text{target}}(q_0)
:= \frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{CODATA}}}
        {Q_A(q_0)\cdot\cos\bigl(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q_0)\bigr)}
\approx 0.998 .

The gate. F passes when F_{\text{target}}(q_0)/10 \le |F(q_0)| \le 10\,F_{\text{target}}(q_0) (same order of magnitude, one decade each way) and is refuted otherwise. The operational test |F(q_0) - F_{\text{target}}(q_0)|/F_{\text{target}}(q_0) > 10 is a sufficient condition for failure: it forces either |F(q_0)| > 11\,F_{\text{target}}(q_0) or a sign reversal, both outside the window.

Step 1 — the target has order of magnitude one. Every ladder factor satisfies |c_k u_0^k| \le |c_2|\,u_0^2 \approx 7.3\times 10^{-5}, with the sequence |c_k|\,u_0^k decreasing to the flat asymptote \approx 2.1\times 10^{-13} established by the radius-of-convergence gate. Hence

\Bigl\lvert \ln \prod_{k \ge 2}\bigl(1 + c_k u_0^k\bigr) \Bigr\rvert
\;\le\; 2\sum_{k \ge 2} |c_k|\,u_0^k
\;\lesssim\; 2\times 10^{-4}
\;\ll\; \ln 10 ,

so the correction product lies within a factor e^{\pm 2\times 10^{-4}} of unity: it cannot move the base value Q_A \cos\alpha_{\text{eff}} by even a fraction of a decade. The empirical target evaluates to F_{\text{target}}(q_0) \approx 0.998 (gate witness), consistent with this bound. Order-of-magnitude proximity to the target is therefore an invariant that every faithful candidate for the correction factor must satisfy.

Step 2 — soundness of rejection. F_{\text{target}}(q_0) > 0, and the true kernel — the element whose expansion generates the canonical c_k — evaluates at q_0 to the correction product of Step 1, hence within 2\times 10^{-4} (in log) of order unity and, up to the sub-percent accuracy of the ladder itself (negligible at a decade threshold), to F_{\text{target}}(q_0). Its window ratio is \approx 1 \ll 10: the true kernel passes at any decade threshold, so no false refutation is possible. Contrapositively, a candidate whose magnitude falls outside the decade window has F(q_0) \ne F_{\text{true}}(q_0), and two fibre elements with distinct archimedean evaluations at q_0 are distinct: the refuted candidate is not the true kernel. Rejection is definitive; passage is only necessary — a passing candidate still faces the exact \S 4(c) integer shadows and the \S 4(a) pole-location test.

Step 3 — calibration of the 10\times threshold. Two constraints bound the admissible threshold window.

  1. Lower bound. The gate must not refute legitimate fibre-level candidates whose archimedean evaluations swing between anchor pins: recorded cross-anchor swings reach \approx 3.5\,\% at the c_3 level, while the substrate variable itself shifts by only 2.1\times 10^{-7} (210 ppb) under the proton–muon re-pin, moving the target through the ladder by \bigl(\sum_k k\,|c_k|\,u_0^k\bigr)\cdot 2.1\times 10^{-7} \approx 3\times 10^{-11} in log — utterly negligible. Any threshold well above the few-percent near-match band therefore tests direction, not anchor choice or near-match precision.
  2. Upper bound. The threshold must still catch the geometric-decay direction errors of Step 4, which escape only thresholds \gtrsim 16.

The decade convention 10\times sits inside this admissible window. Finer discrimination is deliberately delegated to the complementary gates, which admit no tolerance at all (\S 4(c)) or a 10^{-6} fibre-level tolerance (\S 4(a)).

Step 4 — non-vacuity: the stabilisation direction obstruction. The canonical refuted precedent is the family of trace-level candidates whose substrate magnitude is a power of the positive-stabilisation weight z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}). For every q > 1 the AM–GM inequality gives q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} > 2, hence 0 < z < 1/2; at the substrate, z(q_0) \approx 0.4993. A candidate with |F(q_0)| = z(q_0)^m after m stabilisations therefore satisfies

\frac{F_{\text{target}}(q_0)}{|F(q_0)|}
\;>\; 0.998 \cdot 2^{\,m},

which exceeds 10 already at m = 4 (where 0.998 \cdot 16 \approx 16.0). Repeated stabilisation can only shrink the magnitude — it can never climb to a target of order unity, let alone to the linking-weight scale \approx 2.5 of the precedent — so the entire family fails the gate for every m \ge 4. \blacksquare
